draft.title: The first Bolshevik decrees
card: The Bolsheviks took power in Petrograd on 25 October 1917 (7 November in the new calendar). The next day, the Second Congress of Soviets passed their first two decrees.
it called on all fighting nations to begin talks for a peace without forced land transfers or payments. It was a call to end the war, not a peace treaty.
it abolished private ownership of land without payment. Estates of the nobility, the Church and the Crown were handed to local peasant committees to share out.
The decrees kept the Bolsheviks' promises of peace and land. They aimed to win support from war-weary soldiers and from peasants, who made up most of the population.
draft.remember: Peace answered the soldiers' wish to stop fighting. Land answered the peasants' hunger for farmland.

a.q: What did the Decree on Land do?
opts: Took large estates without payment and gave them to peasants
Let landowners keep their estates if they paid a new tax
Put all farmland under the control of Bolshevik officials
Bought large estates from nobles and sold them to peasants
a.why: The decree ended private ownership of land without payment, and peasant committees shared out the estates. It did not make the peasants pay, since the land was taken without compensation.
a.clue: Think about who paid for the land, and who received it.

b.q: Why did the Decree on Peace help the Bolsheviks win support in late 1917?
opts: Many soldiers and workers were tired of war and wanted peace
Germany had agreed to its terms before the decree was issued
It ended the fighting at once and left Russia safe from attack
Most peasants wanted the war to go on until Russia had won
b.why: The decree matched the wishes of war-weary soldiers and workers, which won the Bolsheviks support. It did not end the fighting itself, because it only called on nations to begin talks.
b.clue: The decree was a call to talk, not a treaty. Who wanted it?
